_doc: Config for scripts/lint-html-views.mjs (WC7c). Paths are relative to plan-dashboard/. Rule text: docs/standards/html-view-quality.md; digest: docs/standards/html-view-quality-digest.md.
_notes: 2026-07-21 select-menu.css: REQ-010 reading-floor exception for .sm-option / .sm-button. A chapter-picker row is control chrome, not a reading surface (REQ-009) — the same defence as the .cx-body print-parity and right-drawer entries. Both are set to 1.05rem, matching the closed control they replace (the retired #cx-chapter-select), so the list and the button that shows the same string are one size rather than two.

2026-07-26 packages/prose-editor/styles/prose-editor.css: REQ-010 reading-floor exception for .rte-toolbar / .rte-tool at 0.85rem. Same defence as the select-menu entry above — a formatting toolbar is control chrome, not a reading surface (REQ-009); the reading text sits in the editor BELOW the bar and keeps the host's own size. The value is a --rte-font-size custom property, so a host that wants it larger aliases the token rather than overriding the rule.

2026-07-26 walk_roots added so the linter sees packages/ as well as src/. The prose-editor workspace lints at WARN, matching src/components/ — it is a library, not a shipped view, and blocking_paths stays limited to src/pages/ + src/layouts/.

2026-08-06 READING-FLOOR (REQ-010) added — the rule was UNGATED. The two exception notes above were written against a check that `lint-html-views.mjs` never implemented, so forty-plus sub-floor prose selectors went unreported, including four-sentence FAQ answers at 0.92rem on a blocking-path page. Same shape as the INLINE-SCRIPT-BLOCK gap below it. Reports at WARN on every path, for the same reason that one does: the rule accumulated real violations while ungated, and a check that blocks the build the day it is written gets bypassed rather than obeyed; --strict promotes it. Note that `allow` stays EMPTY — both hand-written exceptions above fall out of the rule's own logic rather than needing an entry: select-menu's .sm-option/.sm-button are chrome selectors, not prose elements, and prose-editor's .rte-tool reads `var(--rte-font-size)`, which the check refuses to resolve rather than guess. It scores only `rem` and `px`; var()/calc()/clamp()/%/em are skipped. `th` and `label` are deliberately outside the prose set — REQ-010's own EXEMPT list covers mono-uppercase column heads, and a `label` here is form chrome. Remaining open findings are mostly the print-parity family (blockquote.quran p.tr, figcaption) which is the book edition's deliberate typographic hierarchy, plus the workbench and Composer confirm-list — all left visible rather than waived, so they stay a per-view decision.

2026-08-04 INLINE-SCRIPT-BLOCK (D-DoD) added — the DoD's 'no inline <script> bodies' half was never gated while the <style> half was, so the linter reported clean over a 1,067-line script in src/pages/intelligence.astro. It reports at WARN on every path, including the blocking ones: extracting each script changes how that page hydrates and is discussed one page at a time. To silence a single file once its script is deliberate, add an allow entry 'INLINE-SCRIPT-BLOCK — <reason>'.
